note: Open upstream issues that explain an oracle expectation wallet-backend does not meet. A failing oracle check that matches a rule is labelled with the issue; one that matches none is reported as unexplained, which is a candidate new finding. Rules match on the expected row and on where the oracle saw the change; they never hide a failure. A rule's earlier_reports lists issues filed before the labelled one that describe the same defect or part of it (#806: factory deploys only; #805: failed transactions only); the label is the issue whose scope covers every case the rule matches. A rule with `fixed_by` labels a defect wallet-backend has since fixed, and only at commits that are git ancestors of that fix (in the clone the harness builds from), so the same failure at a later commit stays unexplained; the backtest still counts such a failure as a failure (`fixed_upstream` in the oracle verdict).

rules.title: An XLM transfer through the native asset contract that creates the destination account gets no ACCOUNT CREATE state change
Contract deployments that no auth entry declares get no ACCOUNT CREATE state change (factory deploys, Stellar Asset Contracts)
A pre-authorized transaction signer that core removes in txChangesBefore never gets a SIGNER REMOVE state change
A pool-share trustline removed by an authorization revocation gets no TRUSTLINE REMOVE state change

Transaction meta participants are silently dropped: participantsForMeta reads only TransactionMeta's v0 arm, so an account an operation changes but does not name (a sponsor whose sponsorship ends, the maker of an offer taken whole) is not a transaction participant
Participants taken from the envelope: a failed transaction's operations: payment destinations and other addresses its envelope names (fixed in 9538b3c)
Participants taken from the envelope: an account only an authorization entry names, which no require_auth matched (fixed in 9538b3c)
Participants taken from the envelope: a contract the meta never shows: the invoked contract, event emitters, a declared deploy (fixed in e2da4ca)
Participants taken from the envelope: a state change for a contract a declared deploy would have created, which the meta does not create (fixed in 80121f3)
